flag.summary: Segments built as a Position=First|Middle|Last axis composed in an auto-layout row, not as fixed composites per segment count.
flag.why: MUI composes positionally — it assigns firstButton / middleButton / lastButton classes by child index and drives all the radius and seam CSS off those classes. A Position axis is the same model, and it lets designers add or remove segments freely; the story alone uses both 2-segment and 3-segment groups, so a fixed composite per count would have needed two components on day one.
flag.tradeoff: Figma cannot assign a variant property by child index. A designer who inserts or reorders a segment must update Position by hand, and a wrong Position puts the seam and the pill cap in the wrong place. A fixed composite would have made that impossible but would not scale past the counts shipped.
flag.reuse: Every one of the 54 segments is a CLONE of the corresponding Variant=Contained Button variant, so padding, typography, label, icon slots and state colours are Button's validated internals rather than redrawn rectangles.

MUI renders that as Select -> Menu -> Popover Paper -> MenuList -> MenuItem, so the parts are real and shipping even though no story exercises them directly.
flag.handling: No standalone Select component was built — it would duplicate Text field's Select boolean, which already IS the closed control. Menu / Item and Menu were built, sourced from MenuItemOverrides plus MUI substrate rather than from a story. This is the second documented exception to structure-from-argTypes, after TextField's Size axis.

flag.summary: MUI's Select diverges from a plain outlined TextField in three ways, and Tebra's icon replacement adds a fourth.

divergences.detail: nativeSelectSelectStyles gives the outlined select element paddingRight: 32, overriding OutlinedInput's input padding of 14, to reserve space for the icon. Text field's Select boolean cannot vary padding by boolean, so its text clearance stays 14 — the same limitation class as Button's icon padding pull.

MUI places the select icon at right: 7 with color action.active and top: calc(50% - .5em). Tebra replaces the icon component wholesale via TextFieldOverrides SelectProps.IconComponent, so none of that applies: the Tebra caret uses right: 4%, color grey[600], top: calc(50% - 12px).

right: '4%' is a PERCENTAGE, so the inset scales with field width. Figma cannot express a percentage inset. Modelled at a stated reference width of 300px, where 4% = 12px. At 600px the real caret sits 24px in; at 200px, 8px. MUI's own 7px would have been width-independent.

MUI's select icon rotates 180 degrees when open (`ownerState.open && { transform: 'rotate(180deg)' }` in nativeSelectIconStyles). Tebra's replacement is a plain styled(DownCaretIcon) that never receives ownerState, so THE TEBRA SELECT CARET DOES NOT ROTATE WHEN THE MENU OPENS. Autocomplete's popup indicator does rotate, because AutocompletePopupIndicator handles it. The two dropdowns in this library behave differently on open.

flag.handling: All four transcribed into the Text field description and here. No Open axis was built on the closed control, because with a non-rotating caret there is no visual difference between open and closed.

flag.summary: The Menu's list padding is 0, not MUI's 8 — and it disagrees with the Autocomplete listbox.
flag.detail: ListOverrides.ts sets MuiList defaultProps disablePadding: true globally. MenuList renders a List, so the Menu paper has zero vertical list padding. The Autocomplete listbox is a styled div, not a List, so it keeps MUI's padding '8px 0'. Two dropdown surfaces in the same library, 8px apart.
flag.handling: Menu built with padding 0, Autocomplete listbox left at 8. Reported, not harmonised — the fix is a code decision.

flag.summary: Menu's elevation 8 shadow is pure MUI substrate — the Tebra theme never defines a shadows array.
flag.detail: createTheme is passed only palette, typography and components, so all 25 elevations are MUI defaults. Only three are actually reached by this library: 1 (Paper default, Autocomplete listbox), 3 (referenced directly by AlertOverrides), and 8 (Popover default, which Menu inherits). Nothing in the theme reviews or overrides any of them.
flag.handling: Elevation / 1, 3 and 8 created as bound effect styles translated layer-for-layer from theme.shadows. See figmaBuild.overlayRecipe.

flag.generator: tokens-page-generator.js, alongside this schema. THE GENERATOR NOW EXISTS ON DISK — it did not before 2026-08-03, which is the only reason the page was ever allowed to go stale. Five steps, each run as its own use_figma call: clear+header, colour, typography, dimension, verify. Only one value is hand-substituted (<DATE> in step 1); everything else is derived from the file.
flag.summary: The Tokens page is a generated, read-only rendering of the three variable collections. Do not hand-edit it.
flag.lastRegenerated: 2026-08-03 — full rebuild from the live collections after tier 6 left the page reporting 62 colour / 31 dimension against 67 / 32. Recovered the five missing swatches: illustrationTeal, illustrationCream, uaDefaultLinkBlue (hardcoded), alphaBlack04, alphaBlack12 (computed). illustrationTeal now renders #004952 in red in the hardcoded group, which is the whole reason that variable exists. flag.regenerate: Whenever any variable collection changes. Run the five steps in tokens-page-generator.js in order. The generator reads collections live via getLocalVariableCollectionsAsync / getLocalVariablesAsync and derives every swatch, specimen, bar, group membership, ordering and header count from them, so a regenerated page cannot drift from the variables. Hand edits will be destroyed on the next run — step 1 clears the page frame's children first.
flag.authoredNotDerived: Four things in the generator are authored constants rather than reads, and are the only places the page can go stale on its own: the colour GROUP_ORDER list, the two '(no palette)' group captions, the ALIASES map, and the typography blurb. A group not in GROUP_ORDER is appended last and REPORTED in the return value as unplacedGroups; a dimension prefix that is not space/radius/border/size is reported as unplaced. Neither is ever silently dropped.
flag.boundNotPainted: Swatch fills bind their own variable; spacing bar widths, component-size rule heights, corner radii and stroke weights all bind theirs (18 width + 7 height + 16 radius + 12 stroke-side bindings, 0 failures). Only values Figma cannot bind — hex strings, var() syntax, px numbers, brand aliases — are rendered as text. Verified 2026-08-03: 569 solid paints, 0 unbound; 0 fractional authored dimensions.
flag.aliasSource: Brand aliases (Growth 1, Vitality 0, Synapse ramp, Backbone, Core, Siren/First aid/Remedy, Energize/Neuron, Restore/Cyto/Vigor, Practice/Circadian) are transcribed from the trailing comments in paletteValues.ts. The generator keys them BY LITERAL, not by token name — that is how secondary/contrastText and core/contrastText, which carry no comment in source but hold #004852, resolve to 'Growth 1'. 41 of the 47 palette-group colours have an alias; the other 6 render without one because no commented literal matches. Note tokens.color['secondary.100'].tebraName in this schema reads 'vitality 4' while source reads 'vitality 4, used for disabled' and the page renders 'Vitality 4 (disabled)' — the schema copy is the abridged one.

flag.summary: Four variables carry no WEB code syntax. All four were added in tier 6; every variable created before then has one.
flag.detail: The two tier-4 hardcoded orphans (chipSuccessBackground, chipErrorClickableHover) deliberately carry their raw hex as WEB code syntax, so the token layer shows a bare literal among var() entries. The three tier-6 hardcoded colours carry nothing at all, and space/40 carries nothing while every other space token has var(--tebra-space-N).
flag.handling: NOT resolved unilaterally — setting a code syntax is a token-layer edit, and for space/40 the plausible value var(--tebra-space-40) would be invented rather than transcribed (see flags.tebraCssVarsDoNotExist). The generator renders the gap instead of hiding it: a colour with no code syntax falls back to its own hex literal in red, which is visually identical to the deliberate tier-4 convention; a dimension token with no code syntax renders 'no code syntax set' in red. So the page is honest either way.
flag.decisionNeeded: Daniel: set the three hardcoded colours to their hex literals to match the tier-4 convention, and decide whether space/40 should carry a var() at all.

flag.summary: The var(--tebra-*) code syntax on ~112 variables does not correspond to any CSS custom property in web-app-v2. Nothing in the source defines or reads those names.
flag.evidence: grep -rE '--tebra|cssVarPrefix|CssVarsProvider' over packages/design-system/src returns 0 matches; the same grep over the whole checkout returns 0 files. The theme is built with createTheme (not experimental_extendTheme / CssVarsProvider), so no CSS variables are emitted at all — emotion writes literal values into generated class names.
flag.impact: The code syntax is a Figma-side naming convention invented during this build, not a transcription from source. It reads as a promise that a developer can type var(--tebra-color-primary-main) and get the token; today they cannot. It also makes the flags.chipLiteralsBecameVariables phrasing — 'because there is no CSS variable to point at' — misleading, since it implies the other 112 do point at one.
flag.handling: Reported, not changed. This is a real disagreement between the Figma token layer and the code, which is the deliverable; it is not a bug to normalise. Options if it is ever resolved: strip the code syntax entirely, restate it as the JS path (theme.palette.primary.main), or ship the CSS variables in web-app-v2 and make it true. Do not quietly delete 112 code syntax entries.

flag.summary: The floating-label notch was faked with a background-coloured chip masking the border; rebuilt as a genuine gap in a three-slice outline.
flag.detail: MUI's NotchedOutline is a fieldset whose legend interrupts the top border. The original build simulated that with a background.paper-filled frame sitting on top of a stroked rectangle. That only reads correctly on white — on background.default #E8E5DF, cards, or the canvas it showed as a white chip floating on the border.

sourceGeometry.capLeftDerivation: NotchedOutlineRoot borderWidth 1 + padding '0 8px' -> the legend box starts 9px in
sourceGeometry.labelXAgreement: 9 + 5 = 14, which is exactly InputLabel's outlined shrunk transform translate(14px, -9px) — the two derivations agree independently
sourceGeometry.fieldsetTopOffset: top: -5 with legend height 11 — the legend straddles the border so the visible outline still lands on the input box at y=0. The -5 is the mechanism, not a different result; the 56px height is unaffected.

flag.handling: Rebuilt on all 10 Text field variants and all 30 Autocomplete / Field variants. Label slot hidden when the label does not float. The gap sizer is bound to the Label text property so the notch tracks custom labels. Verified on a background.default surface.

flag.summary: Both fields were filled with background.paper, but MUI's OutlinedInput declares no backgroundColor — the control is transparent.
flag.detail: OutlinedInputRoot sets position, borderRadius and border-colour rules only. Nothing paints a background. The paper fill was an unexamined assumption carried from the first build, and it is what let the fake notch look convincing.
flag.handling: Both Text field and Autocomplete / Field are now transparent, so the surface behind shows through the notch gap and the control body. Tag keeps its white fill, which IS Tebra (ChipOverrides.outlinedPrimary). Easily reverted if a filled input is wanted as a design decision, but it would be a decision, not a transcription.

flag.summary: Cloning a variant that already lives inside a COMPONENT_SET silently drops every componentPropertyReferences on the clone and its descendants.
flag.detail: The 10 cloned Small variants had zero references while their Medium sources had 10 each. Nothing errors: setProperties on an instance still records the value, the variant just has no node listening, so the override appears to do nothing. Caught only because a validation instance rendered default text instead of the label that had been set.
flag.handling: Repaired by walking the source and clone trees in lockstep and copying references node-for-node (95 restored). Audited every other set afterwards — Button, Field, Option and Tag were all built by adding properties AFTER combineAsVariants, so none were affected. Recorded in pluginApiNotes.

flag.summary: The notch gap sizer must reproduce every node that widens the visible floating label, not just the label text.
flag.detail: With Required=true the visible notch became [Label][Asterisk] at 81px while the gap slot, sized only by the label text, stayed 72px — so the asterisk sat outside the gap and overlapped the border. Only surfaced on the Error+Required combination.
flag.handling: Added an 'Asterisk sizer' to the Label slot bound to the same Required boolean. Gap now tracks in all four Size x Required combinations (93/93 without, 102/102 with).

flag.summary: The one Tebra-authored TextField element positions itself with a percentage, so its inset scales with field width.
flag.detail: TextFieldOverrides' GrayDownCaretIcon uses right: '4%' and top: calc(50% - 12px). The percentage means a 600px field puts the caret 24px from the edge where a 300px field puts it 12px — Autocomplete's equivalent indicator uses a fixed right: 9. The -12px vertical offset also assumes a 24px icon while fontSize='small' resolves to 20px intended / 22.86px computed.
flag.handling: Transcribed at a fixed 12px inset and vertically centred, with both quirks recorded in the component description.

flag.summary: Naming a TEXT node 'Text' is a no-op, so Figma auto-renames it from its content.
flag.detail: 'Text' is already the default name for a new TEXT node, so assigning it does not clear the node's autoRename flag; the subsequent `characters` assignment overwrites the name. A notch label intended to be called 'Text' came out named 'TextField Label' and broke a name-based lookup. Autocomplete / Field has the same latent inconsistency but was wired by index so it never surfaced.
flag.handling: Set a TEXT node's name AFTER its characters, and never to the literal 'Text'. Recorded in pluginApiNotes.

flag.summary: The Akkurat LL Medium->Bold substitution does not affect any style in the typography.ts ramp.

The only place a 500 weight appears is MUI's ListSubheader default (fontWeightMedium), which drives the Autocomplete group label and is not part of the Tebra ramp.

flag.summary: LinearEllipsisIcon draws a VERTICAL three-dot stack — a kebab / MoreVert — despite its name.
flag.detail: All three circles share x=12.29 and step down y at 4.29 / 12.0 / 19.71; the path's bounding box is 4.57 wide by 20 tall. The separate EllipsisFilledIcon is the horizontal one (three dots inside a circle).

flag.summary: MUI sets flexWrap:'wrap' on the Autocomplete inputRoot, so multiple selected values wrap onto extra rows and the field grows.

flag.summary: The chip delete icon is full-strength primary.main because Tebra overrides it — MUI's own default would be a muted 70% (and 26% for filled chips).
flag.detail: MUI Chip gives outlined+coloured chips a deleteIcon at alpha(palette[color].main, 0.7), and filled chips alpha(text.primary, 0.26). ChipOverrides.deleteIcon sets color: theme.palette.primary.main with no alpha, and theme styleOverrides are appended after MUI's base styles, so Tebra wins.
flag.reviewNote: Raised in review as 'should be ~26% muted'. That is the MUI default, not what ships. The saturated teal is a deliberate Tebra override; the glyph and size were the real defects.

flag.summary: Outlined chips ship a full-strength primary.main border, not MUI's alpha(main, 0.7).
flag.detail: ChipOverrides.outlinedPrimary sets border: 1px solid primary.main and backgroundColor white. MUI's outlined chip is transparent with a 70% border. Both are Tebra overrides that win.

flag.summary: Every illustration in the design system is drawn in #004952, which is not the palette teal. paletteValues primary.main, primary.dark, info.dark, action.active and action.focus are all #004852 (growth 1).
flag.where: All seven SVGs in src/components/illustrations. 405 of the 490 colour usages across the set.
flag.detail: The two differ by one step in the green channel: 0x48 = 72 vs 0x49 = 73. A grep for 004852 across the illustrations directory returns zero files, so no illustration ever uses the palette value. The difference is visually imperceptible, but it is the reason the art cannot bind to color/primary/main without changing a rendered value.
flag.effect: The dominant brand colour of the illustration set is off-token. Any future attempt to recolour illustrations from the palette produces a diff on 405 paths, and any audit assuming the illustrations use brand tokens is wrong.
flag.handling: Built as it ships. Promoted to color/hardcoded (no palette)/illustrationTeal so every path still binds and the value renders red on the generated Tokens page, which is the established mechanism for a colour with no palette entry. Not silently snapped to #004852 — that would change rendered output.

flag.summary: #F8F3EB appears once, in NothingToSeeHereIllustration, and matches no palette entry.
flag.detail: The nearest palette neighbours are action.selected #F0EEE8 (backbone 2) and background.default #E8E5DF (backbone 3). It is neither. The naming pattern suggests a backbone 1 that paletteValues.ts does not define.
flag.handling: Bound to color/hardcoded (no palette)/illustrationCream. Reported, not normalised.

flag.summary: Three ReadMore stories pass isInline where the component prop is $isInline, so the inline behaviour they document never happens.
flag.where: ReadMoreAlert.stories.tsx args, ReadMoreMaxCharacters.stories.tsx args, ReadMoreMaxLines.stories.tsx argTypes.
flag.detail: ReadMoreProps extends EllipsisTextProps, which declares $isInline, $maxLines and $maxCharacters — the $ prefix keeps them off the DOM. Story args are assigned as a plain property on the story function and are never checked against ReadMoreProps, so the unprefixed spelling compiles silently. With $isInline undefined, EllipsisText renders display: -webkit-box rather than inline, and the leading space before the button — gated on ($isInline || !isCollapsed) — is skipped too.
flag.effect: Two of the four ReadMore stories carry a docblock stating that the button sits inline with the text on a single line. That is not what renders; the button drops onto its own line.
flag.handling: To be built as it ships, with the button on its own line. The intended inline arrangement is described in the component description but not depicted, because no story actually produces it.

flag.summary: NotFoundErrorMessage renders "submit a support caseor contact customer support" — the space between the link and the following sentence is lost.
flag.detail: The source closes at the end of one line and continues "or contact customer support" on the next. JSX strips newlines adjacent to a tag, so the two text runs concatenate with no separator. Both siblings get this right with an explicit {" "}: InternalServerErrorMessage after each , ForbiddenErrorMessage after its . NotFoundErrorMessage is the only one of the three that omits it.
flag.handling: To be built with the space present — depicting a text bug as a design decision would be worse. Flagged for the bug list.

flag.summary: ForbiddenErrorMessage links with a raw <a> while its siblings use MUI <Link>, and the package styles no <a> at all, so the two render in different colours.
flag.where: ForbiddenErrorMessage.tsx (raw <a> to the Tebra Help Center) against NotFoundErrorMessage.tsx and InternalServerErrorMessage.tsx (MUI <Link>).
flag.detail: There is no MuiLink override in src/overrides, and CssBaselineOverrides defines only *:focus-visible and *:focus:not(:focus-visible) — no anchor rule anywhere in the package. A raw <a> therefore falls to the user-agent default, conventionally #0000EE with a solid underline, while MUI Link resolves to primary.main #004852 underlined at alpha 0.4. The same sentence pattern, two link treatments, in sibling components of one family.
flag.handling: Both to be built as they resolve. Reported as a disagreement, not harmonised.

flag.summary: InternalServerErrorMessage ships <Link>contact support</Link> with no href, directly below a TODO saying the link is missing.
flag.detail: MUI Link without href renders an anchor with no href: not focusable, not keyboard-reachable, but still carrying full link styling. The comment immediately above reads "TODO: Add a link to the contact support".
flag.handling: To be built as styled text, matching what renders. Recorded in the component description.

flag.summary: ReadMore asks for color="inherit" but the theme forces primary.main at rest, so "inherit" only takes effect on hover — the label goes from teal to black.
flag.detail: MUI sets color: inherit in its base styled() when color="inherit". Tebra ButtonOverrides.text sets color: primary.main and is appended after the base at equal specificity, so the theme wins at rest. StyledButton then adds "&&:hover, &&:active { color: inherit }", whose doubled specificity wins it back on hover. The result is a resting label at #004852 that turns text.primary #000 on hover, over the primary[100] #CBDDE0 hover background the same theme rule supplies.
flag.effect: A colour inversion on hover that nobody appears to have chosen: the component asked for inherit in every state and receives it in exactly one.
flag.handling: Both states to be built as they resolve.

flag.summary: The six Feedback messages share one skeleton and disagree on nearly every measurement in it.
flag.detail: Stack marginTop is 0 (NoResults, NotFound), 16 (NothingToSeeHere) or 24 (Forbidden, InternalServerError, BrowserIncompatibility). Stack spacing is 8 (NoResults, NothingToSeeHere) or 16 (the other four). An h4 text.secondary eyebrow above the title is present in three (NotFound, Forbidden, InternalServerError) and absent in three. The h2 title carries sx maxWidth 45ch in three (NoResults, NothingToSeeHere, BrowserIncompatibility) and no constraint in the other three, while all six constrain the body to 75ch. Two carry an action Button, four carry none. One writes padding={5} where the other five write p={5}.
flag.handling: All six to be built as they ship, as six values of one Variant axis. Reported as the disagreement set, not normalised — the fourth recurring-surface finding after the four list-row surfaces, the five interactive states and the five disabled greys.

flag.summary: The Illustrations stories pass width/height whose aspect ratio does not match the viewBox, so the catalogue renders the art squashed — while the Feedback messages size the same art proportionally.
flag.where: src/stories/Illustrations/*.stories.tsx args against the Box dimensions in src/components/Feedback/*.tsx.
flag.detail: NotFoundIllustration has a 524x440 viewBox, ratio 1.191. Its story passes width 285 / height 184, ratio 1.549. The SVGs declare no width or height of their own, only a viewBox, so an outermost svg stretches to whatever box it is given. The messages avoid this: NotFound is sized 337x283 (64.3% of the viewBox, ratio preserved), NothingToSeeHere 455x262 (96%, preserved), and AccessRestricted, Error and BrowserIncompatibility are sized to their viewBox exactly.
flag.handling: Masters built at the viewBox — the undistorted shape, and the one the product actually renders. The story sizes are recorded but not built.

flag.summary: Of the seven illustrations, two are unused by any Feedback message, two have no Storybook story, and one serves two different messages.
flag.detail: AlmostThere and Waiting are exported and unused inside the design system; both are consumed downstream by signin-ui and clinical-notes-ui. Waiting and BrowserIncompatibility have no story, and BrowserIncompatibility is the only illustration used by a message yet missing from the catalogue. NotFoundIllustration serves both NotFoundErrorMessage and NoResultsMessage, so a "no results" state shows the 404 artwork.
flag.handling: All seven built as masters, since all seven are exported from the package. The usage map is recorded in each component description.

flag.summary: The Feedback message text widths are declared in ch, a unit with no Figma equivalent and no value derivable from component source.
flag.where: sx maxWidth 45ch on three titles and 75ch on all six bodies.
flag.detail: 1ch is the advance width of the digit zero in the element own computed font, so 45ch at h2 24px and 75ch at body1 16px are two different pixel values, both dependent on Akkurat LL metrics. Deriving them means reading a font metric rather than a component value; measuring them in a browser is forbidden by the method.
flag.handling: Unresolved. The honest options are to bind a fixed text width and record it as a Figma-only approximation, or to let the text hug and document the constraint. Deferred to the resumed batch rather than guessed.

flag.summary: InternalServerErrorMessage onRefreshClick builds a URLSearchParams, deletes redirectUrl from it, then discards it and calls window.location.reload().
flag.detail: The computed searchParams is never read again and never written back to the location, so the redirectUrl stripping has no effect — the reload preserves the query string the code was trying to clean.
flag.handling: No visual consequence. Recorded for the bug list.

flag.summary: The Figma family pages file five components differently from the Storybook titles those same components ship under.
flag.where: Figma figmaBuild.pages._order vs the story titles recorded in coverageSweep.
flag.detail: Storybook files Icon button, Toggle button and Read more under Components/Data Display, Link under Components/Navigation, and Dialog under Components/Feedback. The Figma pages file them by design semantics instead: Icon button, Link and Read more on Actions; Toggle button on Inputs; Dialog on Surfaces & navigation. Storybook's Data Display group is doing duty as a catch-all — it also holds Divider, Typography and the Icon catalogue — so it is a weak signal of what a component is.
flag.handling: Design semantics chosen by Daniel 2026-08-03 when the two taxonomies were put side by side. Recorded, not normalised: this is a code↔design disagreement of the same kind as the four list-row surfaces. Anyone navigating between Storybook and the Figma file should expect these five to sit in different groups.

flag.summary: The facesheet card header divider is written as an sx CSS shorthand with a theme path inside it, so the whole declaration is invalid and no divider renders.
flag.where: facesheet-ui/src/components/Card/FacesheetCard.tsx:217 and facesheet-ui/src/components/Card/CardLayout.tsx:170 — the only two occurrences of this pattern in the monorepo.
flag.detail: sx={{ borderBottom: "1px solid background.default", height: "3rem" }}. In sx, a full CSS shorthand string is passed through verbatim; only standalone properties like borderColor resolve theme paths. 'background.default' is not a valid CSS <color>, and an invalid value inside a shorthand invalidates the entire declaration, so border-bottom is dropped rather than falling back to a default colour. The intended colour is background.default = #E8E5DF (Backbone 3).
flag.effect: Two of the eight header bands are the only ones that ask for a divider, and neither draws one. The rendered result is identical to the six clinical-system bands, which makes the divergence invisible in a browser and only findable in source — exactly the case the 'never measure from a rendered component' rule protects against.
flag.fix: borderBottom: 1, borderColor: 'background.default' — or a theme callback: borderBottom: (t) => `1px solid ${t.palette.background.default}`.
flag.handling: Reported, not fixed — web-app-v2 is a read-only reference checkout. Do NOT draw a divider on the Figma band until Daniel decides whether the divider or its absence is the intended design; six of eight sites currently ship without one.

flag.summary: One facesheet card implementation sets CardContent paddingBottom to 128px where its twin sets 16px, because a bare number in sx is a spacing multiple, not pixels.
flag.detail: facesheet-ui writes sx={{ paddingBottom: 16 }}. paddingBottom is in paddingKeys (@mui/system/esm/spacing.js:43), so it routes through createUnaryUnit(theme,'spacing',8,'spacing') (spacing.js:85). theme/theme.ts passes createTheme only palette, typography and components — no spacing key — so createSpacing falls back to its default of 8 (createTheme/createSpacing.js). 16 x 8 = 128px. The clinical-system twins write sx={{ padding: "0 16px 16px 16px" }}, a string, which is taken literally as 16px.
flag.effect: The same card surface has an 8x difference in bottom padding between two live implementations. 128px is almost certainly not intended — the number 16 reads as pixels at a glance, which is how it survived.
flag.handling: Reported. Relevant to Figma only insofar as the card content padding must not be transcribed from facesheet-ui; use the clinical-system 0/16/16/16 values, which match the MUI substrate's 16px.

flag.summary: ImmunizationsCard hardcodes the drawer card style but still renders the fullscreen-only header band, so in fullscreen it is the only facesheet card with no elevation and no min-height.
flag.detail: Its six siblings wrap in StyledCard (Facesheet.tsx:21-27), which branches on layout: FULLSCREEN gives minHeight 10rem, anything else gives boxShadow none. ImmunizationsCard instead writes <Card sx={DRAWER_CARD_STYLE}> where DRAWER_CARD_STYLE = { boxShadow: 'none' } (types/facesheet.ts:203-205) — unconditionally — and then gates its CardHeader on layout === FacesheetLayout.FULLSCREEN. So in fullscreen it shows the title band on a flat, short card while every sibling is elevated and at least 160px tall.
flag.handling: Reported. Does not change the band spec itself.

flag.summary: Five facesheet cards exist in two live implementations in different packages, and the two disagree on the divider, the content padding and whether the header renders at all.
flag.where: clinical-system/src/components/Facesheet/Cards/* (consumed by FacesheetDrawer.tsx and FacesheetPage.tsx) vs facesheet-ui/src/components/Card/FacesheetCard.tsx (consumed by facesheet-ui CardLayout.tsx).
flag.detail: Medications, Vitals, Labs, Problems and History are implemented in both. clinical-system additionally has Immunizations and Allergies; facesheet-ui additionally has Recommendations and Supplements. Divergences: (a) facesheet-ui declares a header divider, clinical-system does not; (b) facesheet-ui's CardContent bottom padding resolves to 128px, clinical-system's to 16px; (c) clinical-system gates the header band on FULLSCREEN layout, facesheet-ui renders it always; (d) clinical-system's AllergiesCard renders no band at all.
flag.handling: Reported as a disagreement, not normalised — this is the fifth recurring-surface finding after the four list-row surfaces, the five interactive states, the five disabled greys and the six link treatments. Which implementation is canonical is a product question. The Figma band should be built once, from the shared geometry (48px, h2/primary, 16px horizontal), with the divider left off until the question is settled.

flag.summary: There is no MuiCardHeader, MuiCardContent or MuiCardMedia override anywhere, so every card-header decision lives in per-site sx.
flag.where: packages/design-system/src/overrides — CardOverrides.ts, CardActionsOverrides.ts and CardActionAreaOverrides.ts are the only Card-family files.
flag.detail: MuiCard sets defaultProps only (variant elevation, square false, raised false). MuiCardActions sets justifyContent flex-end. MuiCardActionArea sets disabled true — open decision 4. Nothing themes the header. The 48px band, the h2 primary title and the divider are therefore product conventions, not design-system truth.
flag.handling: This is the finding, not a defect: the header band is a de facto pattern with no home in the theme. If it is meant to be a design-system component, the theme is where it should live. Recorded for Daniel to decide; see components.CardHeaderBand for the buildable spec.

flag.summary: The primary nav bar renders under createPartnerTheme, never under the canonical design-system theme, so no part of it is design-system truth.
flag.where: navigation-ui/src/root.component.tsx:37 mounts CobrandedApp; navigation-ui/src/components/CobrandedApp.tsx wraps App in ThemeProvider with the cobranding theme; navigation-ui/src/context/CobrandingContext.tsx defaults to createPartnerTheme('tebra').
flag.detail: createPartnerTheme (design-system/src/cobranding/createPartnerTheme.ts) builds a distinct theme that remaps palette.action.hover, palette.text.primary, palette.background.paper and palette.divider from a NavigationPalette, and adds the only MuiToolbar override in the entire system. schema.decisions.1_sourceOfTruth already scopes src/cobranding out as 'partner navigation chrome only'. The consequence had not been drawn: it puts the whole primary nav outside the design system.
flag.decisionNeeded: Whether the nav bar belongs in the Figma library at all. If yes, cobranding must come into scope and the library gains a second palette with six base themes. If no, the nav should be named explicitly as out of scope on the Cover so it stops resurfacing.
flag.handling: Reported, not resolved — this is a scope question for Daniel. Spec captured in components.PrimaryNavBar in case the answer is yes. UPDATE 2026-08-03: the Tebra-default nav was built anyway, as its own section with every component description carrying the 'renders under createPartnerTheme, not the design-system theme' provenance line. Building it does not answer the scope question — it makes the answer visible. The six-theme surface stays out of the canonical claim.
flag.status: BUILT 2026-08-03 under the scope caveat; publish still gated.

flag.summary: Three nav colours have no home in paletteValues.ts — the same class of finding as the hardcoded Chip hexes.
flag.detail: #195b63 (navIconHoverBackground and submenuBackground and searchResultsBackground), #002328 (searchInputBackground) and #003840 (primaryDark) return zero matches in palette/paletteValues.ts. #004852 and #417E86 do resolve, to Growth 1 and Growth 2. So the Tebra nav is two-thirds palette colours and one-third values that exist only in the cobranding file.
flag.handling: Recorded. If the nav is brought into scope these three need either promotion to the palette or the same 'hardcoded (no palette)' treatment the Chip hexes got on the Tokens page.

flag.summary: Clicking the user avatar opens a completely empty MUI Menu on top of the real hover-driven user menu.
flag.detail: <Menu anchorEl={userMenuAnchor} open={Boolean(userMenuAnchor)} onClose={handleUserMenuClose} ...></Menu> has no children. The avatar's onClick is handleUserMenuOpen, which sets userMenuAnchor and therefore opens this empty Menu — an empty paper plus a modal backdrop that has to be dismissed. The actual UserMenuContent is delivered separately through NavIconButton's menuContent prop, which renders it in its own hover-driven Popper. So the click path and the hover path are different mechanisms and the click path renders nothing.
flag.handling: Reported. Either give the Menu its UserMenuContent children or drop it and the userMenuAnchor state entirely, since the Popper already covers the interaction.

flag.summary: Four console.log calls ship in the navigation render path, three of them explicitly labelled Debug.
flag.where: navigation-ui/src/context/CobrandingContext.tsx (three, inside the useMemo, logging active partner, partner config and theme.palette.primary) and navigation-ui/src/components/Navigation/Navigation.tsx onClickAwayListener (console.log(event.target)).
flag.detail: The CobrandingContext trio run on every partner change and are preceded by the comment '// Debug: log active partner and theme colors'. The Navigation one fires on every click-away while the mobile search is open.
flag.handling: Reported. No visual consequence.

flag.summary: The nav mixes a magic-number media query with theme breakpoints, and forces a 64px bar at every width instead of MUI's responsive 56/64.
flag.where: navigation-ui/src/components/Navigation/Navigation.tsx — isDesktopNav uses useMediaQuery('(min-width:1100px)') while isSmUp uses theme.breakpoints.up('sm'); the Toolbar sets sx minHeight:64.
flag.detail: 1100px matches no breakpoint in the theme, so the desktop/drawer switch cannot be reasoned about from the token set and will not move if breakpoints are retuned. Separately, theme.mixins.toolbar gives 56px below sm and 64px at sm and up; the sx minHeight:64 flattens that, so the mobile bar is 8px taller than the substrate intends.
flag.handling: Recorded. Relevant to Figma only if the nav comes into scope — it means one 64px bar covers every breakpoint, which simplifies the build.

flag.summary: The partner theme's nav icon hover-colour rule does nothing in five of the six base themes, including Tebra's.
flag.where: design-system/src/cobranding/createPartnerTheme.ts MuiIconButton root — '&:hover svg { color: submenuText }' — against baseThemes.ts.
flag.detail: The rule swaps the glyph from navText to submenuText on hover. In tebra-default, blue-dark, blue-light, green and orange both values are #ffffff, so nothing changes; only gray-light differs (navText #969696, submenuText #ffffff). The visible hover feedback in every other theme comes from the background swapping to navIconHoverBackground, not from the glyph.
flag.handling: Recorded as a dead-rule finding in the same family as ToggleButtonOverrides' JSS ref syntax — valid and executing, but with nothing to do. Not a defect; it exists for gray-light.

flag.summary: The partner theme silently REPLACES two canonical styleOverrides roots rather than merging with them, because both sides are functions.
flag.where: design-system/src/cobranding/createPartnerTheme.ts MuiIconButton.root and MuiMenuItem.root, against overrides/IconButtonOverrides.ts and overrides/MenuItemOverrides.ts.
flag.detail: createPartnerTheme calls createTheme(defaultTebraTheme, partnerThemeOverrides), which deep-merges. deepmerge cannot merge two functions, so the later one wins outright. Consequences: the nav's IconButton loses the canonical color grey[600], the canonical hover/active background rule and the disabled grey[500]; the nav's MenuItem loses the canonical focus-visible treatment entirely (white ground, 3px primary.main border, radius 4) and its Mui-selected rules. Sibling keys survive normally — sizeSmall, colorPrimary and colorError are plain objects and merge, which is why the replacement is easy to miss.
flag.effect: The file's docstring says only navigation-specific styles are overridden and all standard component overrides are preserved. For these two roots that is not what happens.
flag.handling: Reported, not resolved. It is why Nav / Icon button and Nav / Menu item are built as separate components rather than variants of the canonical ones — the divergence is structural, not cosmetic.

flag.summary: Tokens page group captions did not wrap, so any caption longer than the 1272px content width was silently clipped.
flag.detail: mkText leaves textAutoResize at its WIDTH_AND_HEIGHT default, so the caption grew past the frame; the page root sets clipsContent true, so the overflow was invisible rather than obviously broken. Surfaced when the hardcoded (no palette) caption was extended to name createPartnerTheme.
flag.fix: Generator now sets textAutoResize 'HEIGHT' and layoutSizingHorizontal 'FILL' on every group caption. Applied to the generator on disk and to the rendered page, so it cannot recur.
flag.handling: Fixed at source, not just on the page.

flag.summary: The Tebra wordmark hardcodes its fill in a <style> block, so it is the one bar element that cannot respond to a partner theme.
flag.detail: #f7f4eb appears nowhere in packages/design-system, and is one step off illustrationCream #F8F3EB without being it. Every other glyph in the bar uses currentColor and therefore follows navText. Recorded as color/hardcoded (no palette)/navLogoCream — a fourth nav orphan alongside #195b63, #002328 and #003840.
flag.handling: Transcribed as authored. Not a defect for Tebra-default, where the cream reads correctly on Growth 1 — but a partner using a light nav ground would get a near-invisible wordmark, which is presumably why PartnerLogo swaps the whole component for an for non-Tebra partners.

flag.summary: The legacy library nav expectation list names nine slots; source ships six, and three of the nine do not exist.
flag.detail: Source order is Platform, Clinical, Billing, Engage, Tebra Payments, Analytics. Against the legacy list: 'app switcher' is Platform under another name; 'reports' is the analytics item, whose config id is analytics but whose glyph component is ReportsIcon; 'patients' and 'history' have NO nav slot at all — patients are reached through the inline search, and there is no history item in the config; 'engage' ships in source but is absent from the legacy list; 'mail' and 'help' are right-cluster utilities, not nav slots.
flag.handling: Source wins, per the batch instruction. Built as the six config items plus the utilities. Reported, not reconciled — the legacy list is a checklist, not a source.

flag.summary: The billing slot can render one of three glyphs; only the default is built.
flag.where: navigation-ui/src/utils/menuBuilder/billingMenuBuilder.ts returns BillingKmbAlertIcon or BillingKmbIcon in place of BillingIcon depending on KMB state.
flag.detail: Both KMB variants use viewBox 0 0 27 22 — a third distinct viewBox in the nav set — and BillingKmbIcon contains a hardcoded <circle fill="#004852">, i.e. a Growth 1 literal baked into the glyph rather than inherited. A NavigationIcons test asserts the KMB plus glyph stays white for contrast, so the two-tone treatment is deliberate.
flag.handling: Not built. The billing slot ships Icon / Billing, the default. Recorded so the gap is known rather than discovered later.

flag.summary: The search magnifier is a trailing adornment in source; the review note described it as leading.
flag.detail: The field sets endAdornment to a fragment of params.InputProps.endAdornment followed by <InputAdornment position="end"><SearchOutlined /></InputAdornment>. There is no startAdornment anywhere in the component. forcePopupIcon={false} and disableClearable remove the dropdown arrow and clear button, so the magnifier is the only adornment and it sits on the RIGHT.
flag.reviewNote: Daniel's review described a leading magnifier. Source is unambiguous on this one, so source won and the icon is built trailing — flagged rather than silently reconciled, per the precedent that review notes get verified against source before being acted on.
flag.handling: Built trailing. If the product genuinely renders it leading, that is a code/product divergence worth its own look — but nothing in this component produces a leading magnifier.

flag.summary: There is no history or clock slot in the primary nav bar. The history-shaped thing in the product is the Recent patients panel inside the search dropdown.
flag.detail: Checked five ways after the height saga's lesson about trusting absence. (1) navigation.config.ts declares exactly six items: platform, clinical, billing, engage, tebraPayments, analytics. (2) useNavigation merges those six ids with six dynamic hooks and nothing else — there is no seventh slot and no fallthrough. (3) A monorepo-wide grep for AppBar and <Toolbar across every package returns ONE file, Navigation.tsx, so there is no second bar rendering alongside. (4) No nav-item registry or injection mechanism exists; messages-ui's NavigationConfig is its own side menu, not the primary bar. (5) useRecentChartsQuery — the only history-shaped data in navigation-ui — is consumed ONLY by PatientSearch, where recentCharts become recentPatientOptions and render as a 'Recent patients' subtitle2 heading plus a Divider inside the search dropdown when the input is under two characters. No icon, no clock, no bar slot. UserMenuContent carries only OpenInNewIcon.
flag.conclusion: Absence confirmed by positive evidence, not by a failed grep. The observation was real; the element is the Recent patients panel in the search dropdown, which is not built (only the closed field is).
flag.handling: Reported either way as asked. Nothing added to the bar. The Recent patients dropdown panel is a candidate if the search states are ever built out.

flag.summary: The nav avatar is built as initials, but initials are the product's fallback — the typical fill is an illustrated persona SVG.
flag.detail: Navigation renders <Avatar src={userImageUrl}>{userInitials}</Avatar>; on image error it swaps to getDefaultUserImage(hasRole(ROLES.Provider)), which returns /shared-assets-ui/bundle/css/img/chrome/persona/provider-tebra-bg.svg or staff-tebra-bg.svg. The initials child only surfaces when the image itself fails to load. So the typical avatar is illustrated content chosen by role, and the built Content=Letter variant represents the fallback.
flag.handling: Recorded on the Nav / Bar description rather than rebuilt: the persona SVGs are runtime assets in shared-assets-ui, outside packages/design-system, and are not transcribed. Content=Letter stays as the built representation.

flag.summary: The nav has no separate Selected state — hover, focus and menu-open are one flag and one paint.
